checklist.notes: The past-continuous examples and station scenario are compatible with A2.1, but the task language repeatedly uses unsupported terms such as ‘recipient’, ‘relay’, ‘less direct’, ‘courtesy’, ‘prominent’, and ‘allow a pitch change’.
The past-continuous form/meaning contrast, timetable language, request forms, and primary stress description for information are accurate.
The timetable notice, polite staff request, and response expectations are natural for the scenario.
No unexplained internal copying was detected beyond the authorized request frame and target forms; no external comparison was made.
The lesson introduces past continuous, word stress, mediation, and the authorized request chunk while using only the declared past, syllable, reading, and writing prerequisites.
The learner-facing language is English and all embedded identifiers are authorized directly or through the prerequisite closure.

methods: Manual comparison of lesson wording with the supplied authoritative request and project-authored teaching payload.
Exact contiguous-word overlap comparison across the ten supplied v3 lesson bodies.
Inspection of the accepted audit provenance/copyright scope without consulting external sources.
copyright_originality_check.scope_limitations: No suspicious unexplained copying was found within the supplied scope. Reuse of target forms, short pedagogical frames, and project-authored definitions/examples is expected. No external search was performed; this is not a plagiarism clearance or copyright guarantee.

findings.description: Sections 2–4 explain core mediation, pragmatics, and pronunciation through dense B1-or-higher metalinguistic vocabulary and clause structure. With no definitions or L1 support, an A2.1 learner may not understand the instructions needed to perform the target tasks.
findings.recommendation: Use concrete role labels (‘your friend’), short verbs (‘tell’), numbered checks, and a simple stress demonstration; gloss or translate necessary technical terms.

limitations: Review used only the exact lesson, accepted audit, regenerated hash-matching authoritative request, and verified M5 development snapshot; generator reasoning and prior review records were excluded.
No audio was supplied; pronunciation judgments cover written instructions and IPA only, not realized speech or learner performance.
No external CEFR vocabulary profiler or corpus was used; CEFR findings are qualitative independent AI judgments about the learner-facing text.

Originality checking was limited to the supplied authoritative payload and the ten supplied v3 lessons; no Internet, external corpus, or plagiarism search was performed, so no external plagiarism or legal-clearance claim is made.
